verdict.summary: Upstream provider latency on the Codex gpt-5.6-luna path. Five ws_close_1011 upstream failures at 03:41-03:49Z, then four reissued turns each held 2251-2377 seconds and released in near-FIFO order at 04:29-04:33Z. All affected runs carried 231k-247k input tokens.

likely_cause.primary: Provider-side capacity or queueing on the Codex gpt-5.6-luna endpoint
likely_cause.aggravator: Seven concurrent Luna runs on one account, each re-submitting 230k-250k input tokens per turn, roughly 1.6M tokens of aggregate prefill demand per fleet round
supporting_signals: ws_close_1011 cluster confined to the five highest-context Luna runs inside a nine-minute window
uniform ~39-minute release in submission order, the signature of a draining queue rather than per-request timeouts
investigator's own Claude request returned rate_limit_error at 04:37:17Z, showing live account-level rate pressure
post-compaction turns cost more at equal context than pre-incident turns did

recommended_immediate_action.detail: Do not restart, interrupt, close, or re-prompt any audit run. Restarting discards up to 60 minutes of context and forces a fresh 240k-token prefill against the congested endpoint, which would worsen the incident.

unverified_boundaries: Provider-side queue state is inferred from client-observed timing and WebSocket close codes; no provider telemetry available
ws_close_1011 read as upstream internal error per the WebSocket specification; the specific upstream fault is not visible from captured metadata
The account rate-limit link is corroborating, not proof of a shared limiter between the Anthropic and Codex paths
